title: The chain orders groups by the DAG and any group id works (GitHub issue #13)
objective: Groups are ordered by the DAG everywhere groups are ordered - a group after every group holding a ticket its own tickets depend on, otherwise by creation - so a group id is only a name.
outline: core/chain.py: order (replacing _gnum and the number sort), sequence, cycle, a creation-key helper and a waits-for helper. ticket_controller.py: only these lines - advance_groups' loop header `for g in sorted(snap.groups.values(), key=lambda x: int(x["id"][1:]))`, idle_lines' `sorted(snap.groups, key=_gnum)` and can_still_start's `_gnum(dgid) < _gnum(gid)` (keep a key for ticket ids, e.g. dagmod._order_key). tickets.py: cmd_list's group sort and main()'s `re.fullmatch(r"g\d+", args.id)` routing. board.py: the `sorted(snap.groups.values(), key=lambda g: int(g["id"][1:]), reverse=True)` of the tickets tab and group_order(). ticket_creator.py: group_problems' pos() check (replace it with a cycle check over the hand-in applied to a copy of the snapshot) and groups_section's filter and sort. prompts/creator/02-rules.md, README. Do not edit set_group, start_issuer, _start_job, land or close_open in ticket_controller.py, nor decide() and ack() in ticket_creator.py: a ticket of group new-g1 changes them.

notes: Group new-g2: the DAG tickets (this order, `actl dag`, revise with DAG) change chain order and group membership together; this one goes first (the other two depend on it, they use chain.order and chain.cycle). The order is 'prerequisites pulled ahead' (depth-first by creation key), chosen because the issue asks that a dependency move the other group ahead (g75 before g63) rather than slide g63 behind every group created before g75. The natural id tie-break keeps today's order for pools and fixtures whose groups share a created stamp or have none. A cycle can only come from hand edits (the opener and `actl dag` refuse one); order() breaks it without raising. Measured 2026-11-24 on today's code with throwaway loop-harness cases: the g62a crashes and the g1->g2 end-to-end behaviour quoted in acceptance 5 and 6. Never write the reporting project's name in code, tests or comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids it in every non-markdown file): say 'the reporting project'.
acceptance: core/chain.py: group B waits for group A when a ticket whose 'group' is B depends directly (dag.json depends_on) on a ticket whose 'group' is A, A != B, neither ticket landed or cancelled, neither group landed or cancelled. order(snap) lists the groups that are not landed or cancelled: taking them by creation key - the group's 'created' (missing = ''), then its id in natural order (runs of digits compared as numbers, a digit run sorting before a text run at the same position: g2 < g10, g62 < g62a < g63) - it places, for each group in turn, first every group it waits for that is not placed yet (recursively, by the same key), then the group itself. A cycle never raises: a group already being placed is skipped. holds, waits_for, behind, behind_line and with_behind keep their meaning on top of this order.

core/chain.py adds sequence(snap): the landed and cancelled groups by creation key, then order(snap); and cycle(snap): None when the waits-for relation has no cycle, otherwise one cycle as a list of group ids in which each waits for the next and the last equals the first, starting at the group with the smallest creation key that lies on a cycle (g1 and g2 waiting for each other, g1 created first: ['g1', 'g2', 'g1']).

Fixtures (core.pool.Snapshot; every group open unless stated; created '2026-11-20T00:00:0<k>Z'; each ticket ready with its 'group' set): F1 g1(k=1) {#1 depends on #2}, g2(k=2) {#2}, g3(k=3) {#3}: order ['g2', 'g1', 'g3'] and waits_for(snap, 'g1') == 'g2'. F2 g63(k=1) {#1 depends on #3}, g64(k=2) {#2}, g75(k=3) {#3}: order ['g75', 'g63', 'g64'] and behind(snap, 'g75') == ['g63', 'g64']. F3 g10(k=1), g9(k=2), no dependencies: order ['g10', 'g9']. F4 g1(k=1) {#1, #4}, g2(k=2) {#2, #3}, #3 depends on #1 and #4 depends on #2: cycle(snap) == ['g1', 'g2', 'g1'] and order(snap) holds g1 and g2 once each without raising. F5 g1 landed (k=3), g2 cancelled (k=1), g3 open (k=2): sequence(snap) == ['g2', 'g1', 'g3']. (Today: F1 and F2 come out in number order, F3 as ['g9', 'g10'], and sequence and cycle do not exist.)

Every sort of groups uses this order: ticket_controller.py advance_groups (sequence), idle_lines (sequence; landed and cancelled groups still give no line), can_still_start (an earlier group = earlier in order(data)); tickets.py list (sequence, --all included); board.py the 整合分支 table (sequence reversed: newest first, as today) and the 整合分支 filter options (sequence); ticket_creator.py groups_section (order(snap), every group id, not only g<N>). No code sorts groups by int(id[1:]) or by the digits of the id any more; core/pool.next_group_id stays g<largest N + 1>.

A group id that is not g<N> works: with ticket #1 ready (needs_verifier false) in open group 'g62a' (created set): `tickets.py list` exits 0 and prints a line starting 'g62a'; `board.py html --out F --query tab=tickets` exits 0 and F contains 'g62a'; one ticket_controller.py run exits 0 with #1 and g62a landed; `tickets.py cancel g62a --why w` (fresh pool) exits 0 and g62a is cancelled. tickets.py sends ready, cancel and rerun to the group path for any id that is not a whole number (ticket ids are whole numbers); the refusal for a ticket id given to rerun keeps today's text ('rerun is for a group g<N>, not for ticket N'). (Today, measured 2026-11-24: list, board and controller exit 1 with "ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '62a'"; cancel g62a exits 2 with 'no ticket g62a in the pool'.)

End to end: ticket #1 in open group g1 depends on #2 in open group g2 (both groups created the same second, both tickets needs_verifier false): one ticket_controller.py run (no --forever) exits 0; #1 and #2 are landed; #1's group is still 'g1' and g1 is landed (not cancelled); no group other than g1 and g2 exists; g1's first 'regression started' event is not earlier than g2's 'landed' event. (Today, measured 2026-11-24: #1 leaves g1 with 'member #1 left: it cannot start in g1', g1 is cancelled and #1 lands in a new group g3.)

The opener's group check follows the same order: ticket_creator.group_problems no longer refuses a ticket placed in a group numbered before its dependency's group; it refuses a hand-in only when its placement makes the waits-for relation (the pool's tickets plus the new tickets in their groups, new groups made last) a cycle, with the sentence '<key>: group <g> makes the group order a cycle: <path>' where <path> is the cycle (as chain.cycle gives it) joined with ' -> '. Case: #1 ready in open g1, #2 ready in open g2 depending on #1, fake creator action 'into_g1_after_2' (one new ticket into g1 that depends on #2): `ticket_creator.py --request x` exits 1, the decision page's lines include '- new-1: group g1 makes the group order a cycle: g1 -> g2 -> g1', and no ticket #3 is written. (Today that line reads '- new-1: group g1 comes before g2, the group of #2 it depends on'.)

The user asked for all of these (2026-11-24: 「OK 照這樣開票」), and ruled on the DAG part in docs/DECISIONS.md D-096 (read it first). ## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
